lesson.title: Changing Text Case
lesson.driving_question: How can a program make text comparisons and labels consistent?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Normalising and displaying text with lower and upper case methods
lesson.concept_budget: Apply lower() and upper() as separate one-operation assignments; other cleanup methods are deferred.
misconceptions: lower() returns changed text and does not alter the original value automatically.
upper() changes letters but not digits.
A normalised value should be stored before it is compared.
lesson.progression_note: Begins the Grade 7 text extension after the shared Grade 6 review and the existing cleaning-text lesson.

shared_program.code:
team = input("Team name: ")
team = team.lower()
code = input("Team code: ")
code = code.upper()
print("Team:", team)
print("Code:", code)

primm.prompt: Recall how a string is stored and how a method call uses a dot and parentheses.
Use Falcons and f7. Predict the two stored values after the method calls and the complete labelled output.
Run with Falcons and f7, then with MIXED Case and ab12. Compare letters and digits in the output.

questions: Why does team.lower() not change team unless the returned text is assigned?
For inputs Falcons and f7, what exact values are stored in team and code before they are printed?
Why does upper() change the letter in f7 but leave the digit unchanged?
What would be displayed for the code if the line code = code.upper() were removed?

primm.prompt: Make the displayed team name uppercase and the displayed code lowercase. Falcons and f7 should become FALCONS and f7.
Add a response input and store response.lower(). Display Accepted when the normalised response equals yes and Not accepted otherwise.
Build a badge formatter. Ask for a first name and a two-letter group code; display the name in lower case and the group code in upper case on separate labelled lines.
Repair the missing parentheses and store the upper-case result before it is displayed.
